Priya: quick repro: single-request runs look normal; failures concentrate in batched runs and include truncated clause completions and extraneous 'see below' lines.
Priya: evidence: diff of outputs from batch vs single on same prompts — bogus tail tokens present only in batched runs.
Mateo: hunch: batching + new int4 kernel + tokenizer tweak
Priya: ran a small diff. tokenizer change in https://git/redwood/tokenizer@c3f4 removed unicode-normalize step for performance. snippet:
```
- text = unicode_normalize(text)
+ text = text  # skip NFKC to shave 5ms
```
Priya: root cause hypothesis: skipping normalization changed token boundaries for em-dash/ellipses -> different tokenization lengths -> KV-cache index mismatch in the int4 batched path. int4 kernel's cache-alloc path didn't zero an extra slot when sequence lengths vary -> stale cache tokens appended to output in batch decoding.
Mateo: that explains why single-request is OK (no batching) and why we see hallucinations not present in earlier evals.
Priya: evidence: reproducer attached (small script) that toggles normalization + batching -> failure rate jumps to ~20% for failing prompts.
Priya: immediate mitigations:
- rollback quant profile to int4-stable for rw-legal-2.13 (low-risk)
- re-enable NFKC normalization in tokenizer patch (tests needed)
- add canary gating: disallow model+quant combos where nightly-eval delta hallucination > 3% from baseline
- add unit tests for em-dash/ellipsis tokenization and a batched KV-cache sanity test
- run extended nightly eval with focused legal-forms subset after rollback
